capability.write-tests-first: Starts a behaviour change by verifying the expected result.
capability.verify-work-results: Confirms the result with checks that were actually run.
capability.plan-implementation: Breaks a requirement into sequential, executable tasks.
capability.debug-root-cause: Establishes the original cause of a failure.
capability.clarify-requirements: Clarifies the goal, the boundaries and the acceptance criteria.
capability.review-code: Brings in an independent review of a defined change.
capability.apply-review-feedback: Fixes confirmed review findings and checks the consequences.
capability.isolate-workspace: Separates a new change from other work.
capability.integrate-branch: Integrates a finished change into the agreed branch.
capability.parallelize-tasks: Runs independent tasks at the same time.
capability.delegate-subagent-tasks: Hands clearly bounded tasks to other executors.
capability.minimize-code-surface: Keeps the implementation to the smallest complete set of changes.
capability.execute-plan: Executes the agreed plan task by task, with check evidence.
capability.author-agent-instructions: Writes and verifies the instructions that steer an agent behaviour.
capability.harden-validation: Adds checks at every data boundary after the cause is removed.
capability.read-large-artifacts: Reads large artifacts in parts without overflowing the context.
capability.redact-sensitive-data: Replaces sensitive values with placeholders before sharing.
capability.diagnose-agent-behavior: Establishes from evidence what happened during the work.
capability.consult-guidance: Checks for applicable guidance before acting.
capability.automate-rule-enforcement: Moves mechanically checkable rules into automation.
capability.communicate-concisely: Delivers the result concisely and on the point.
capability.define-output-format: Fixes the exact sections, order and fields of the result.
capability.audit-codebase: Rates the whole repository by the impact of the findings, not by one change.
capability.manage-technical-debt: Keeps deferred shortcuts in a ledger with their review conditions.
capability.design-structure: Ability to choose the data shape, module boundaries and interaction structure before writing code.
capability.make-states-unrepresentable: Ability to move the rules for valid states into a type and constructor so an illegal state cannot be created.
capability.measure-performance: Ability to measure a metric reproducibly and explain the number together with the baseline and variance.
capability.design-experiments: Ability to compare design or instruction variants on the same tasks and the same criterion.
capability.write-technical-prose: Ability to write technical prose that answers in the first paragraph and carries no template noise.
capability.explain-subsystem: Ability to explain part of a system through its purpose, its boundary and its main execution path.
capability.build-verification-harness: Ability to build and maintain scenarios that prove the product's observable behavior.
capability.triage-reports: Ability to classify incoming reports and findings and route each by class.
capability.coordinate-program: Ability to split large work into parts with an owner, dependencies and merge points.
capability.keep-decision-trail: Ability to record a decision with its options, grounds and review condition.
capability.research-primary-sources: Investigate a question against the sources that own it and record cited findings.
capability.model-domain-language: Sharpen the project's shared terminology and record the decisions about it.
capability.teach-with-workspace: Teach a concept over sessions using a stateful workspace.
capability.author-setup-scripts: Generate an interactive script that walks a human through a manual procedure.
capability.make-retries-idempotent: Makes a state-changing call safe to retry by honouring an idempotency key.
capability.ship-a-change-safely: Keeps a release small and frequent so that risk and debug cost stay low.
capability.treat-runtime-content-as-untrusted: Treats content produced at runtime as data to report, never as an instruction.
capability.define-quality-bar: Records the project's quality bar as a written contract with numbers, commands, and exceptions.
capability.degrade-gracefully-under-failure: Replaces a crash with a safe default, a warning, or a degraded result.
capability.instrument-production-code: Adds logging, metrics and traces to code so production behaviour is visible and diagnosable.
capability.decide-on-deprecation: Decides whether to deprecate a system and whether the deprecation is advisory or compulsory.
capability.migrate-consumers-off-the-old-system: Moves consumers from the old system to its replacement one at a time and verifies each move.
capability.migrate-a-data-schema: Migrates a live data schema in reversible additive phases with a tested down path.
capability.simplify-code: Rewrites code for clarity without changing what it does.
capability.curate-context: Chooses what the agent reads, in what order, and how much of it.
capability.design-user-interface: Builds the user-facing surface: components, states, accessibility and fit with the design system.
capability.evaluate-dependencies: Judges a dependency or an upgrade by size, maintenance state, risk and licence.
capability.generate-idea-variations: Generates and compares distinct options for an idea before one of them is chosen.
capability.hand-back-the-next-step: Ends the turn at a confirmed boundary and hands the choice of what happens next back to the user.
capability.harden-security-controls: Applies security controls to code that handles untrusted input, secrets and permissions.
capability.manage-dependency-supply-chain: Keeps third-party dependencies audited, reproducible and inside a committed script policy.
capability.manage-personal-data: Classifies, minimises, retains and deletes personal data.
capability.find-the-project-tooling: Finds the exact framework and library versions a project runs on before acting on them.
capability.disagree-with-reasons: States a technical objection with its concrete cost and an alternative, and accepts the human's override.
capability.audit-accessibility: Audits an interface against accessibility requirements: keyboard operation, accessible names, contrast, and signalling that does not rely on colour.
capability.reuse-cached-sources-safely: Reuses a stored result only after the origin confirms it is unchanged and the parameters that produced it stay visible.
capability.improve-performance: Removes the cost that a measurement proved dominates a path — query plans, indexes, connection pools, caches, payload and rendering — and guards the metric it moved.
capability.detect-the-run-mode: Establishes from the signals in a session whether the run is interactive or unattended, and defaults to the mode that keeps a present human in control.
capability.facilitate-a-group-discussion: Runs a discussion in which several perspectives each argue their own case in one shared exchange.
capability.check-for-name-collisions: Detects a new entry whose key would silently replace an existing one and puts the collision to the owner.
capability.assess-change-impact: Judges how far a significant change reaches across the requirements, the design, the interface and the operations.
capability.guide-a-human-review: Guide a human through a body of work one block at a time and pace the work on the signals the human gives.
capability.write-configuration-override: Author a configuration override that changes the behavior of an installed skill for one layer of users.
capability.stress-test-a-product-concept: Tests a product concept by describing the finished product and answering the hardest customer and stakeholder questions before anything is built.
capability.never-invent-what-was-not-stored: States only what the record holds and names the gap instead of filling it with invention.
capability.distribute-a-package-of-skills: Ships a set of skills and personas as one installable unit that carries its own record, its own announcements and its own retirement list.
capability.write-a-design-contract: Writes the design as two peer documents: a visual identity with machine-readable tokens and an experience document with behaviour, states and journeys.
capability.persist-work-to-disk: Keeps every intermediate result in a file so a run survives being interrupted and nothing is lost between the conversation and the artefact.
capability.handle-an-authentication-prompt: Turns an authentication or authorisation demand from an external service into a short human interaction: stop the task, state the exact step, verify the credentials, retry, and record it as normal flow rather than as a defect.
capability.capture-an-idea: Writes a forward-looking idea down at once, with its rationale, its trigger and its place in the codebase, without gating the capture on questions.
capability.profile-the-working-style: Derives a profile of how the user works from observed sessions and states the confidence of each dimension.
capability.automate-what-can-be-automated: Set up and run everything the agent can do itself — commands, servers, databases, environment variables, tools, credentials — and leave only human judgement to the human.
capability.scope-tool-reach: Keeps a powerful capability in the role that needs it and out of the role that does not.
capability.write-knowledge-documents: Writes the documents of a knowledge corpus: the metadata, the body, the provenance, the links and the history that go with them.

pattern.approval-policy-proceed: Approval policy: do the agreed work and stop only at an irreversible step.
pattern.approval-policy-gate: Approval policy: size the work first, then ask for approval.
pattern.approval-policy-choice-proceed: Approval policy choice: proceed with agreed work and stop only at an irreversible step.
pattern.approval-policy-choice-gate: Approval policy choice: size the work first, then ask for approval.
pattern.test-first-development: Verifies the expected behaviour first, then adds the implementation.
pattern.verification-before-completion: Backs every claim with fresh check results.
pattern.implementation-planning: Organises dependent steps into a verifiable plan.
pattern.systematic-debugging: Finds and confirms the root cause before fixing anything.
pattern.requirements-clarification: Establishes the need and agrees the direction before design.
pattern.code-review: Rates a change independently against the requirements.
pattern.worktree-isolation: Separates development in its own worktree.
pattern.branch-integration: Checks finished work before the agreed integration.
pattern.parallel-execution: Runs independent work at the same time without shared state.
pattern.subagent-delegation: Hands a bounded task over and checks its result.
pattern.code-minimization: Satisfies the requirement with the smallest complete change.
pattern.plan-execution: Runs the plan in order, with a decision log and a check per task.
pattern.instruction-authoring: A topic tag for the instructions that write and revise the agent instructions themselves.
pattern.defense-in-depth: Makes the failure impossible with checks on several levels.
pattern.bounded-artifact-reading: Bounds reading and output by the size of the artifact.
pattern.evidence-redaction: Keeps the artifact evidential without its sensitive values.
pattern.evidence-analysis: Analyzes execution artifacts from evidence, not from guesses.
pattern.guidance-selection: Selects applicable guidance before work begins.
pattern.automated-enforcement: Replaces manual reminders with a check.
pattern.concise-communication: Delivers the result without preamble or repetition.
pattern.output-formatting: Fixes the shape of the result before it exists.
pattern.code-audit: Reviews the whole repository in a stable order of impact.
pattern.technical-debt: Makes deferred decisions visible and traceable.
pattern.structural-design: An approach in which the data structure and module boundaries determine the shape of the code.
pattern.state-modeling: An approach in which valid states are described by a type rather than by a set of checks.
pattern.performance-measurement: An approach in which a change is judged by measurement with a baseline and variance.
pattern.experiment-design: An approach in which variants are compared on the same tasks and the same criterion.
pattern.technical-writing: An approach in which technical prose is built around the thesis, an example and the reader's question.
pattern.subsystem-explanation: An approach in which a subsystem is explained from its purpose to its main path.
pattern.verification-harness: An approach in which product behavior is proven by a reproducible set of scenarios.
pattern.report-triage: An approach in which incoming reports are classified and routed by one rule.
pattern.program-orchestration: An approach in which large work proceeds in parts with explicit owners and dependencies.
pattern.decision-trail: An approach in which decisions are recorded together with their grounds and review condition.
pattern.approval-policy: An approach in which the approval policy is chosen by user configuration while both opposite policies are stated explicitly.
pattern.domain-language: An approach in which the project's shared terms are sharpened and used consistently.
pattern.teaching-workspace: An approach in which learning is grounded in a persistent workspace and the learner's level.
pattern.setup-scripting: An approach in which a manual procedure is turned into a guided, verifiable script.
pattern.progressive-disclosure: An approach in which material is placed on a hierarchy so the top stays legible and reference is reached by a pointer.
pattern.completion-criteria: An approach in which every step ends on a condition that tells the executor the work is done.
pattern.expand-contract: An approach in which the shape of the change is widened first: the new form is added, the callers are migrated in batches, and the old form is deleted.
pattern.vertical-slicing: An approach in which work proceeds as narrow complete paths through every layer.
pattern.explore-then-exploit: An approach in which raw material is mined before structure is committed.
pattern.idempotent-retry-design: An approach in which a repeated call applies its effect exactly once.
pattern.untrusted-content-handling: An approach in which only the documented signal is taken from a fetched page and any instruction inside it is never obeyed.
pattern.migration-strategy: An approach in which the migration strategy is one of the alternatives: bridge the old interface for a while, or migrate the callers and delete the old path.
pattern.verification-rerun-policy: An approach in which the policy for re-running a verification check is one of the alternatives: reuse the last successful run, or run the check again at the claim moment.
pattern.test-placement-strategy: An approach in which the placement of a test is one of the alternatives: the cheapest level that still proves the behaviour, or the highest seam available.
pattern.quality-bar-contract: An approach in which the project bar is a written contract that names a number, the command that checks it, and the exceptions.
pattern.bar-weakening-detection: An approach in which the change itself is inspected for the moves that lower the bar.
pattern.deprecation-decision: An approach in which a removal is decided first, then announced, then migrated, then deleted.
pattern.incremental-cutover: An approach in which the number of consumers is moved one at a time: the old and the new run side by side and each consumer is moved over on its own.
pattern.graceful-degradation: An approach in which a failure produces a safe default or a degraded result instead of a crash.
pattern.adversarial-self-review: An approach in which a decision is cross-examined by a fresh context before it stands.
pattern.behavior-preserving-refactor: An approach in which a change rewrites how the code is expressed without changing what it does.
pattern.trust-graded-context: An approach in which every loaded source carries a trust level and instruction-like content inside data is surfaced, not followed.
pattern.design-system-adherence: An approach in which the product's own tokens, components and states decide the surface instead of a generic house style.
pattern.short-lived-branches: An approach in which branches are cut from the trunk, merged back quickly and deleted after the merge.
pattern.failure-first-analysis: An approach in which a failure is assumed and worked backwards to the failure modes that caused it.
pattern.risk-first-ordering: An approach in which the riskiest unknown is built first so the failure is discovered early.
pattern.staged-exposure: An approach in which work that is not ready is merged behind a switch instead of being held back.
pattern.safe-defaults: An approach in which new behaviour is inert or off until it is explicitly enabled.
pattern.revertable-increments: An approach in which every increment can be taken back without touching the ones around it.
pattern.structured-observability: An approach in which records are structured events, correlated to a run and attributed to their entry point.
pattern.symptom-based-alerting: An approach in which alerts fire on user-visible symptoms and carry a runbook.
pattern.control-tiering: An approach in which every control is classified as always applied, needs approval, or is never done.
pattern.supply-chain-gating: An approach in which dependency installation and updates pass an audited gate.
pattern.data-minimization: An approach in which only the fields that are needed are collected and emitted.
pattern.threat-modeling: An approach in which the points where untrusted data enters are mapped and the trust boundaries, assets and abuse cases are reasoned about before controls or findings are enumerated.
pattern.release-readiness: An approach in which a change clears an explicit readiness checklist before it reaches users.
pattern.metric-gated-decision: An approach in which the next step is decided by thresholds on observed metrics.
pattern.prepared-reversal: An approach in which the way back is prepared and timed before the change goes out.
pattern.operational-telemetry: An approach in which every signal exists to answer a named operational question.
pattern.project-conventions-first: An approach in which the project's own commands and conventions are found and used before any work starts.
pattern.source-cited-decisions: An approach in which each framework-specific decision comes from the current official documentation and carries its source.
pattern.specification-gate: An approach in which the specification is written, saved and approved before planning or coding starts.
pattern.living-specification: An approach in which the specification is updated before the code follows a changed decision.
pattern.testable-criteria: An approach in which a vague requirement is rewritten as a concrete, testable condition.
pattern.stop-on-conflict: An approach in which a contradiction between two governing sources stops the work until it is resolved.
pattern.reasoned-disagreement: An approach in which a technical objection is stated with its concrete cost and an alternative.
pattern.accessibility-compliance: An approach in which an interface is judged against a fixed list of accessibility requirements.
pattern.standing-quality-bar: An approach in which a fixed project-wide bar is applied to every change and is not renegotiated.
pattern.cache-design: An approach in which a cache is justified by measurement, keyed on every varying input, invalidated by one written strategy and bounded in size and staleness.
pattern.query-plan-discipline: An approach in which the query plan is captured before the change and the index is designed for the query shape.
pattern.resource-bounds: An approach in which a shared resource is sized against a hard limit and fails fast when it is exhausted.
pattern.delivery-budget: An approach in which what the client downloads and runs is bounded, deferred and served over a cached fast path.
pattern.test-design: An approach in which each test states its intent in a name, arranges its own state and asserts one specific outcome.
pattern.frozen-intent: An approach in which the human-owned intent is captured in a block of the artifact, is read-only for the agent and is locked once the human approves it.
pattern.matrix-coverage-audit: An approach in which a written behaviour matrix is audited against the tests that actually ran.
pattern.multi-voice-delivery: An approach in which several voices are woven into a single exchange instead of listed as separate answers.
pattern.preserved-disagreement: An approach in which a disagreement is left standing instead of being reconciled into a consensus.
pattern.dialectical-discussion: An approach in which participants are pushed against each other until the clash produces something no one of them would have reached.
pattern.uneven-voices: An approach in which the participants are not equal and the spotlight moves from round to round.
pattern.collaborative-dialogue: An approach in which the reader is drawn into the exchange and a question is returned to them.
pattern.spawn-on-divergence: An approach in which independent agents are brought in only for the rounds where uncoloured disagreement is the value.
pattern.shared-room-context: An approach in which every participant receives the whole exchange and not only the part it answers.
pattern.context-relay: An approach in which a point-to-point channel is supplemented by the lead relaying what a member missed.
pattern.standing-cast: An approach in which the participants stay available for the whole session and are released only at its end.
pattern.change-impact-assessment: An approach in which a significant change is traced through every artifact it touches before a path is chosen.
pattern.concrete-trigger: An approach in which a change request starts from the named event that revealed it and the evidence collected.
pattern.non-blaming-analysis: An approach in which a change is analysed factually, without fault, and the decision stays with the owner.
pattern.halt-on-missing-precondition: An approach in which a run stops with the reason named as soon as a precondition is missing.
pattern.scope-routing: An approach in which the size of a change decides who carries it out and what done looks like.
pattern.dimension-sweep: An approach in which every dimension of the level is decided, deferred or an open question, and none is left silent.
pattern.pinned-stack-table: An approach in which every pinned technology is listed with its version and nothing else.
pattern.verified-loading: An approach in which a nested instruction file is used only after its loading has been checked in every harness in use.
pattern.override-layering: The effective configuration is resolved from several layers by a per-field-kind merge rule.
pattern.source-conversion: An approach in which material written for another tool is read whole, extracted into outcome, consumer, trigger and know-how, and rebuilt rather than copied.
pattern.single-source-of-truth: Each fact is written once, in one owner, and referenced from there instead of copied.
pattern.stable-identity: A work item keeps one identity for its whole life, and that identity is never given to anything else.
pattern.decision-scoped-research: An approach in which the research covers the dimensions that bear on the decision and prunes the rest.
pattern.working-backwards: An approach in which the finished product is described and defended before it is built.
pattern.package-lifecycle: An approach in which an installable unit declares what it contains, what it needs, where to start and what it has retired.
pattern.unattended-execution: An approach in which the run continues without human interaction: no question is asked, an unanswerable question becomes a blocker with a terminal status, and the run always ends with an explicit status.
pattern.exhaustive-path-enumeration: An approach in which every branch and boundary of a change is walked mechanically and only the unhandled paths are reported.
pattern.elicitation-boundary: An approach in which the owner writes the content and the agent draws it out instead of supplying it.
pattern.staged-elicitation: An approach in which the requirements are drawn out broad-first, in a fixed order, before any drafting.
pattern.stakes-calibrated-rigor: An approach in which the depth of the document and the severity of its findings follow the stakes the owner stated.
pattern.two-spine-contract: An approach in which the visual identity and the behaviour are written as two peer documents that reference each other by name.
pattern.impact-based-severity: An approach in which a finding is rated by the impact of leaving it, not by the effort of fixing it.
pattern.named-protagonist-journey: An approach in which a flow is written as a real session with a named person and a climax beat.
pattern.human-in-the-loop: A step that needs a person is marked as such, says which step it is, and is never scheduled as if an agent could do it.
pattern.claim-freshness-window: An approach in which every class of claim carries a maximum age and a source past that age no longer supports it.
pattern.source-hierarchy: An approach in which the source that owns the claim is read before the sources that only describe it.
pattern.finding-severity-policy: An approach in which the findings either carry a severity label or carry none, and the review states which one applies.
pattern.empty-result-policy: An approach in which an empty result is either a valid outcome or a signal to re-check, and the stance is stated in advance.
pattern.failing-test-policy: An approach in which a test that found a defect is kept and marked, against the rule that a failing test is fixed or removed.
pattern.finding-presentation-policy: An approach in which the findings are presented with or without severity labels, and the review states which one it does.
pattern.review-execution-policy: An approach in which the review runs in a separate session or context, against the rule that a review changes nothing.
pattern.review-application-policy: An approach in which the review lenses apply their findings, against the rule that a review only lists them.
pattern.description-shape-policy: An approach in which the description of an instruction is a summary plus trigger phrases, against the rule that it carries only the trigger.
pattern.directive-form-policy: An approach in which a prohibition names the permitted alternative, against the rule that a prohibition is only a hard guardrail.
pattern.rule-authority-policy: An approach in which a rule carries the authority the failure needs, against the rule that guidance is written moderately.
pattern.review-fix-application-policy: An approach in which the review lenses apply their own findings, against the rule that a review only lists them.
pattern.adversarial-empty-result-policy: An approach in which an adversarial review may end with no findings, against the rule that it must always produce findings.
pattern.dependency-readiness: Selects the units that may run now: a unit whose direct predecessors have no completion evidence is named, skipped and reported, and the wave waits for them instead of dispatching it.
pattern.strict-argument-parsing: A keyword is a command only when it is the entire argument; anything else is content.
pattern.evidence-preservation: The evidence of a run is copied into a durable place of its own before the working directory that produced it is removed.
pattern.collision-free-naming: An approach in which every named output slot (heading, flag, identifier) is unique across the installed set, so two producers cannot silently merge into one another.
pattern.ownership-scoped-removal: An approach in which a removal touches only the entries the component stamped as its own and leaves every other entry of the shared file untouched.
pattern.checkpoint-and-resume: A run that cannot finish inside one turn leaves a committed, resumable half-state — the external job, its manifest and the handoff are on disk — so a later run picks the work up instead of repeating it, and the completion record is deferred until the deferred part is verified.
pattern.permissive-conformance: An approach in which the consumer tolerates what it does not know and rejects only what it cannot read.
pattern.trust-signals: An approach in which trust is inferred from objective recorded signals instead of from a score that is stored.
pattern.provenance-record: An approach in which the material a document derives from is recorded with the facts that let a consumer attribute and judge it.
pattern.cross-reference-linking: An approach in which documents are related by links whose kind is stated in the prose around them.
pattern.attested-computation: An approach in which a computed value is produced by a declared computation and checked by deterministic code against the receipt of the run.
pattern.portable-knowledge: An approach in which the knowledge lives in plain files that any tool can read, diff and ship.
pattern.context-degradation-policy: An approach in which the context degradation is detected by the signals of the running session, or by the measured utilisation bands, and the two are alternatives.
pattern.context-degradation-signals: Context degradation policy: react to the degradation signals the running session already shows.
pattern.context-degradation-measured: Context degradation policy: decide from the measured context utilisation bands.
pattern.checkpoint-cadence-policy: An approach in which the verification checkpoints are placed, against the rule that the work is checkpointed once at the end of the meaningful part.
pattern.acceptance-criteria-timing-policy: An approach in which the acceptance criteria are judged, against the rule that they are cleared before the next step starts.
pattern.control-failure-posture-policy: An approach in which a control that cannot load is declared and its failure is loud, against the rule that a hook contract declares the error posture of every step.
pattern.empty-result-posture-policy: An approach in which an empty result is reported as a gap, against the rule that a section with nothing to say is removed.
pattern.finding-shape-policy: An approach in which a finding carries one canonical shape, against the rule that the findings are labelled by their own leverage.
pattern.revision-round-continuity-policy: An approach in which a revision round resumes the same implementer, against the rule that every round runs in a fresh agent.
pattern.delegation-requirement-policy: An approach in which a required delegation that cannot run is done inline, against the rule that a missing capability halts the run.
pattern.working-copy-authority-policy: An approach in which the local tree is the working copy and the remote is its copy, against the rule that the version-controlled copy is the authority.
